purpose: One title-normalisation vocabulary, asserted by BOTH runtimes that implement it.
why_this_file_exists: The rule lives twice, and it has to. supabase/functions/_shared/tools/dj-normalise.ts
owns it for match_key, which is frozen at write (spec 4.1.2) - changing it is a backfill
migration, not a deploy. workshop/workshop/tools/dj_setlists.py needs the same rule at
read time, in Python, on the other side of the courier boundary, over setlist.fm titles
that never pass through Alfred at all. Neither can call the other.
On 2026-09-02 the two disagreed. The Python copy recognised '(Remastered 2012)' and
missed '(2011 Remaster)', so diff_dj_setlists reported Today, Luna and Cherub Rock as
MISSING from the Smashing Pumpkins playlist while all three were sitting in its body -
and two of them then resolved to the exact video_id already recorded there. The suffix
list looked complete because the cases it missed had not appeared yet. The complete list
already existed, in the other language.
So: neither implementation is checked against the other's SOURCE, which drifts. Both are
checked against these CASES. A vocabulary entry added on one side and not the other fails
a test in the runtime nobody edited - the only arrangement that survives someone who has

note: Asserted by BOTH runtimes: isVariantCut() in dj-normalise.ts, _VARIANT_RE in
dj_setlists.py. Same duplication that let the qualifier vocabulary drift (spec 14.6),
pinned the same way so it does not get a second chance.
SEPARATE FROM THE QUALIFIER VOCABULARY ABOVE, AND THEY DISAGREE ON PURPOSE.
Qualifiers answer 'are these the same song for GROUPING' and are frozen at write.
This answers 'is this recording a variant cut' at READ time. 'instrumental' is here
and deliberately absent there: an instrumental cut is plausibly a distinct recording
worth counting on its own, and is still not what a setlist entry is asking for.
Two callers: the resolver refuses to resolve a setlist entry to a variant (12.11 rule 2),
and 12.10's cram tie-break makes a variant stand down when a studio cut of the same
title is in the playlist - you learn a song from the studio recording.

⚠️ A KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The word 'live' is in the title, so the marker fires on a song that is not a variant of anything. It is tolerable because BOTH callers degrade safely: 12.10's rule only suppresses a candidate when a NON-variant sibling shares its title, and a second recording of this song would also contain 'live' - so nothing is suppressed and the duplicate is reported instead. The resolver is the exposed one: a setlist entry genuinely titled 'Live and Let Die' resolves to not_found rather than to a recording. Fix it with a positional rule (a marker inside brackets or after a dash) if it ever bites; do not widen the vocabulary.
